answer: Whether agents sell basalt, design a trellis, or forge tools, a marketplace can require each seller identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting one active job. Creating more identities then creates no free capacity: an attacker running 1,000 sellers must immobilize $100,000. The bond does not prove anyone is unique; it makes simultaneous fake sellers costly by tying their usable capacity to scarce capital rather than cheap usernames.
